table_title: List the 42 English and British monarchs from William the Conqueror (Norman Conquest, 1066) through Elizabeth II (reign ended September 8, 2022), per the union of Wikipedia's `List of English monarchs` (1066-1707 + Anne 1702-1714 cross-listed) and `List of British monarchs` (1707-present, excluding incumbent Charles III). Universe rule (strict Wikipedia regular-row policy): includes ONLY monarchs listed in the main sequence of both master articles' canonical rows; EXCLUDES the 'Disputed claimant' sections (Empress Matilda 1141, Lady Jane Grey 1553, Louis VIII of France 1216-1217, Edgar Ætheling 1066) and EXCLUDES the Interregnum 1649-1660 (Cromwell-era Lord Protectors not monarchs). Edward V (1483) INCLUDED per main-sequence listing. Philip II of Spain (Philip I of England via jure uxoris co-kingship with Mary I, 1554-1558) INCLUDED per main-sequence listing. Joint-reign split: William III and Mary II staged as 2 separate rows (Mary II 1689-1694 [died], William III 1689-1702 reigning alone 1694-1702). Split-reign merge: Henry VI (Lancaster, two reign segments 1422-1461 + 1470-1471) staged as 1 row (1422-1471 first-accession-to-final-end); Edward IV (York, 1461-1470 + 1471-1483) staged as 1 row (1461-1483). Anne cross-list merge: Anne staged as 1 row (Accession 1702 from English list + End 1714 from British list — she spans both lists across the 1707 Acts of Union). For each monarch, give the Accession Year (first-accession-year for split reigns), End of Reign Year (final-end-year), and Royal House(s) text (free-form to handle split-house cases like George V's 1917 rename from Saxe-Coburg and Gotha to Windsor → 'Saxe-Coburg and Gotha; Windsor').
db_analog: WITH english_monarchs AS (SELECT monarch_name, accession_year, end_of_reign_year, royal_house FROM wiki_list_english_monarchs WHERE NOT is_disputed_claimant AND NOT is_interregnum AND accession_year >= 1066), british_monarchs AS (SELECT monarch_name, accession_year, end_of_reign_year, royal_house FROM wiki_list_british_monarchs WHERE NOT is_disputed_claimant AND tenure_status = 'completed' AND accession_year <= 2022), unioned AS (SELECT * FROM english_monarchs UNION ALL SELECT * FROM british_monarchs), merged AS (SELECT monarch_name, MIN(accession_year) AS accession_year, MAX(end_of_reign_year) AS end_of_reign_year, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT royal_house, '; ' ORDER BY royal_house) AS royal_house FROM unioned GROUP BY monarch_name) SELECT monarch_name, accession_year, end_of_reign_year, royal_house FROM merged ORDER BY accession_year ASC, monarch_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia `List of English monarchs` + `List of British monarchs` master articles, accessed via cycle-2 audit's master-derived 42-row dump on 2026-05-19. Universe is the closed canonical 42-entry English-and-British-monarch completed-reign sequence from William the Conqueror (1066) through Elizabeth II (2022). Benchmark window: completed-reign monarchs only — incumbent King Charles III (acceded September 8, 2022, still reigning as of 2026-05-19) is OUT of scope per the NATO-SG / Chief-Justices precedent; when Charles III's reign eventually ends, universe extends 42→43+. source_count = 2 registered: `List of English monarchs` (William I 1066 → Anne 1707 + Anne 1702 cross-listed) + `List of British monarchs` (Anne 1707 → Elizabeth II 2022). operation_type = union+filter (union of the 2 master lists' main sequences + completed-reign filter + 1066-cutoff filter + strict-Wikipedia-regular-row policy filter excluding disputed-claimant sections). temporal_sensitivity=medium — universe extends when current reign ends. Cycle-2 audit's required staging edits applied at cycle-0: (1) split-reign merge: Henry VI (Lancaster, 1422-1461 + 1470-1471 segments) → 1 row 1422→1471; Edward IV (York, 1461-1470 + 1471-1483 segments) → 1 row 1461→1483; (2) Anne cross-list merge: Anne staged as 1 row with Accession 1702 (English list) + End 1714 (British list) spanning the 1707 Acts of Union; (3) Sort = Accession Year ASC + Monarch ASC alphabetic tiebreak (resolves 3 same-year ties: 1483 Edward V before Richard III; 1689 Mary II before William III; 1936 Edward VIII before George VI); (4) Philip II of Spain Royal House(s) = 'Habsburg' is curator-normalized — Wikipedia master lists Philip jure uxoris but Habsburg label is supplied by per-monarch Wikipedia article context, NOT directly by the 2 master lists' tables; documented as normalization decision. Per-row cells: Monarch name verbatim from Wikipedia per-monarch article canonical titles (e.g., 'William the Conqueror' NOT 'William I', 'Anne, Queen of Great Britain' NOT just 'Anne', 'James VI and I' to reflect Scottish + English numbering, 'Queen Victoria' with title); Accession Year per master tables; End of Reign Year per master tables (for split reigns, final-end-year applies); Royal House(s) free-text per master tables with split-house multi-value cell for George V (rename from Saxe-Coburg and Gotha to Windsor 1917).
_extraction_notes: Temporal instance — closed canonical 42-entry English-and-British monarch completed-reign universe ordered by Accession Year ASC + Monarch ASC tiebreak. Single PK Monarch (names unique within the 42-entry universe per Wikipedia per-monarch article canonical titles). Chips History family from 4 to 5 instances with NEW History/Monarchy subdomain (current History distribution: Politics ×2 + Empires + Military; adds Monarchy). NEW `people/monarchs` fine-class extending people bucket from 16 to 17 instances (joining laureates ×3, scientists ×2, authors ×2, athletes, painters, philosophers, deities, honorees, politicians, astronauts, diplomats, judges). Source plan: 2 registered sources (List of English monarchs + List of British monarchs — universe + value role for all 4 cells per cycle-2 audit's source repair from disambiguation-page fallback). operation_type = union+filter (NOT just filter — the union step combines the 2 master lists). claim_type = source_defined under the strict-Wikipedia-regular-row policy: universe = monarchs listed in the main sequence of both master articles (NOT in 'Disputed claimant' sections; NOT during Interregnum 1649-1660). Cycle arc: 2 rounds of pre-staging design review (cycle-1 'Revise' with 3 BLOCKING — source plan disambiguation-page issue / universe policy / House vocabulary; cycle-2 'Approve With 4 Required Staging Edits' — split-reign merge / Anne cross-list / tiebreak sort / Philip Habsburg curator-normalized). All 4 cycle-2 edits applied at cycle-0 using audit's verbatim 42-row dump. 4-cell schema (Monarch PK + Accession Year + End of Reign Year + Royal House(s)) at 42 rows = 168 source-grounded cell values. Sort: Accession Year ASC + Monarch ASC tiebreak (resolves 1483/1689/1936 ties). Strong LLM-knowability for famous monarchs (William the Conqueror 1066 Norman Conquest, Henry VIII 1509 wives + English Reformation, Elizabeth I 1558 Elizabethan era, Victoria 1837 longest-reign-pre-Elizabeth-II, Elizabeth II 1952 70-year-reign); mid-difficulty for lesser-known (Stephen 1135 Anarchy civil war, Edward V 1483 78-day reign, Philip II of Spain jure uxoris 1554-1558, William III 1689 Glorious Revolution + Mary II joint reign); harder calibration for split-reign / split-house edge cases (Henry VI Lancaster two-segment 1422-1471, Edward IV York two-segment 1461-1483, George V Saxe-Coburg-and-Gotha→Windsor 1917 rename, Anne cross-list 1702-1714 spanning Acts of Union). Temporal category-fit: per the temporal category contract, the row universe is ordered along the calendar-year axis with Accession Year as the canonical ordering attribute — mirror precedent `nato_secretaries_general_birth_country_terms` (Term Start Year), `united_states_chief_justices_by_tenure_start_year` (Tenure Start Year), `nber_dated_us_recessions_since_1929` (Peak Year). 3-cycle audit history total: 2 pre-staging design reviews + cycle-0 staging (post-staging cycle-1 expected per master-verbatim staging pattern).
